findings.neutral_note: Shipped compose files publish backend, frontend and PocketBase ports on all host interfaces (no loopback prefix on the mapping). .env.example describes the host-side bindings as loopback, and the codex-oauth overlay (compose.codex-oauth.yaml:8-9) does use 127.0.0.1 prefixes, but the base compose files do not enforce a loopback binding. Combined with auth disabled by default (L2) this yields default network-reachable unauthenticated API access, including settings surfaces where provider API keys are entered. Remediation direction: bind host-side mappings to loopback by default and require an explicit opt-in for wider binding.

CORS allow_origin_regex is set to match any http(s) origin whenever auth is disabled (the default). Amplifies H1: any origin can call the unauthenticated default deployment. Explicit-origins mode exists when auth is enabled.

FastAPI app is constructed without disabling docs/redoc/openapi.json, and router-level auth dependencies do not cover these built-in routes, so the full API schema remains reachable even in deployments with AUTH_ENABLED=true. Metadata disclosure of the complete route surface.

Partner web-continuity state, which contains a session_key credential, is persisted via plain Path.write_text on a temp file then renamed: the resulting file inherits the process umask (typically group/world-readable) rather than an explicit owner-only mode. Every other secret store in the repo routes through 0600/0700 helpers (see I4). Remediation direction: use deeptutor.utils.secret_files.write_secret_text or an exclusive-create 0600 temp.

cookie_secure defaults to false, so the auth session cookie is issued without the Secure attribute unless the operator opts in; SameSite falls back to lax on plain HTTP. Acceptable for loopback use, weaker for LAN/remote deployments that stay on HTTP.

Authentication is disabled by default (documented localhost-first design; require_auth is a no-op in that mode). Deliberate and documented, but it is the multiplier that turns H1/M1 into default unauthenticated network exposure rather than a loopback-only posture.

Outbound TLS verification can be disabled for provider traffic (opt-in system setting, default off, refused when ENVIRONMENT=prod, warned once). Guardrails exist; residual risk is that non-production opt-in still sends provider credentials over unverified TLS.

The detached-launcher stop handshake token is written to launcher.stop via plain write_text (umask-derived mode), while the adjacent state file that also carries the token uses atomic_write_json (owner-only temp). Local-only impact surface.
The literal 'sk-no-key-required' is used as a sentinel for keyless local endpoints at 11 sites. Intentional placeholder, treated as a non-secret by doctor.py:108/327; not a credential.

Shipped default auth settings seed username 'admin' with an empty password hash, which the bootstrap logic explicitly treats as non-authenticating (deeptutor/multi_user/identity.py:138-157). No default password exists.

Zero provider-shaped key literals (sk-/ghp_/AKIA/AIza/xox patterns) and zero secret-valued os.getenv defaults found in non-test source. Test fixtures use obvious dummy values (tests/services/config/test_model_catalog_secrets.py, tests/core/test_agentic_client_provider_kwargs.py, tests/services/mcp/test_call_failures.py). Locale/banner/label false positives from the generic pass were triaged out.

On-disk secret stores and their write paths inventoried: auth secret and skill-hub tokens via write_secret_text (0600/0700); MCP per-owner secrets under data/system/<owner>/private with explicit owner-only modes; auth users.json, device credentials and grants via atomic writes whose temp files are created owner-only; Codex credentials relocated by rename into the owner-private tree; Invidious tokens under the owner-private tree (0700 dirs); model catalog with plaintext provider keys at data/user/settings/model_catalog (owner-only via exclusive temp create; outside the sandbox-runner mounts per docker-compose.yml:163-167); partner channel secrets in data/partners/<id>/config.yaml (plaintext at rest, masked in read APIs by manager.py:150). Only M3 and L4 deviate from the owner-only pattern.

Host-side restricted-subprocess exec is enabled by default (documented: office-skill document generation works out of the box; stronger runner/bwrap backends take precedence). Documented tradeoff, listed for inventory completeness.
Active redaction/masking helpers observed at these sites (error-body scrubbing, secret fingerprints, masked channel configs, redacted URLs). Positive hygiene inventory.

All 44 AST log-call candidates triaged: every hit logs absence messages, token counts, variable/path names, or pre-redacted values; no call site prints a credential value. Dedup-marked (referenced, not counted): deeptutor/services/pocketbase_client.py:160 and deeptutor/partners/channels/dingtalk.py:249 log exception bodies (scan-log-exception-bodies class; the dingtalk site also misuses {}-style placeholders with stdlib logging); provider response bodies in user-facing errors are covered by fix-provider-body-leak (myfork a8618a063).
